prior_evidence: v1 passed its untouched n=16 usefulness rule but still missed two late-benefit cases whose gap after 64 was 20 and 46. Those outcomes are frozen and are used only to motivate a nonzero exploration/audit floor; no v1 threshold is retuned here.
purpose: Test whether a small pre-outcome randomized audit of would-be stopped challenger branches preserves nonzero support, detects late-benefit tail events, and can improve quality while retaining incumbent safety. This is a support/monitoring experiment layered over the already-frozen v1 policy.
base_policy: Exactly v1: always buy through challenger compile index 65; if certificate, finish full; if no certificate stop at 65 when best_gap>11 else buy through 129; if certificate finish full; if no certificate stop at 129 when best_gap>9 else finish full.

audit_design.decision: For each would-be base-policy stop at checkpoint c in {64,128}, compute SHA256(salt + '|' + family + '|' + decimal_seed + '|' + decimal_checkpoint). Interpret the first 64 bits as unsigned u64; audit iff value < floor(0.2*2^64). The salt was generated and persisted before any v2 holdout outcome was evaluated.
audit_design.audit_action: Override that stop and finish the entire seeded challenger trajectory; retain two-arm incumbent and return min-live verified endpoint.
audit_design.propensity_note: The precommitted salt defines a reproducible Bernoulli-style design. Every base-policy rejected branch has a declared 0.2 audit probability under a uniformly random pre-outcome salt; log the realized selection and never change salt after outcomes.

estimand.missed_gain_in_base_rejections: Sum over base-policy stopped cases of exhaustive challenger gain over two-arm.
estimand.horvitz_thompson: For audited rejected cases only, estimate total missed gain as sum(observed_gain / 0.2). Report realized estimate and exact full-holdout truth separately; do not use non-audited outcomes in the estimator.

co_primary_metrics: Per-case no-harm invariant versus two-arm for base and audited policies
v1 and v2 gain recovery fractions versus exhaustive challenger
v1 and v2 challenger compute fractions versus exhaustive challenger
Number/fraction of would-be stopped cases audited and number of late-benefit cases discovered by audit
HT missed-gain estimate versus actual missed gain, reported descriptively because this 40-case sample is small
predeclared_v2_usefulness: If exhaustive gain is positive, v2 must retain zero harm, recover at least as much aggregate gain as base v1, and use <=50% of exhaustive challenger compilations. Audit-estimator calibration has no pass threshold in this first small holdout.
scope: Synthetic positive-monotone graph 2-CNF ROBDD ordering only. The audit principle is motivated by off-policy support concerns, but this result alone does not validate a general theorem-proving exploration policy.
